narrativeContent.name: Primary Safety Objective
narrativeContent.description: Determine the safety and tolerability of IF001 in previously transplanted recipients of a kidney from a living donor.

narrativeContent.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
narrativeContent.description: Evaluate the efficacy of IF001 in preventing graft loss and BPAR following removal of pharmacologic IS.

narrativeContent.name: Secondary Safety Objectives
narrativeContent.description: Characterize the incidence and grade of acute GVHD by Day 120 and severity of chronic GVHD by one-year post-IF001 infusion. Characterize the incidence of BK viremia, viruria, infection, and nephropathy by 15 months post-IF001 infusion. Characterize the incidence of proteinuria, neurotoxicity, anemia, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, major adverse cardiovascular events, and malignancies. Describe the time from IF001 infusion to neutrophil recovery (>500/µL) and platelet recovery (>20K/µL), the number of blood component transfusions, the incidence of engraftment syndrome, the incidence of primary and secondary hematopoietic graft failure, and the incidence and severity of bacterial, fungal, and viral infections.

narrativeContent.name: Secondary Efficacy Objectives
narrativeContent.description: Evaluate changes in renal function (eGFR by CKD-EPI 2021) from Day −9, prior to the first dose of transplantation conditioning, to Month 15. Evaluate the time to the event for the composite of BPAR, graft loss, death, or lost to follow-up and each component. Describe the correlation of donor chimerism with meeting the primary efficacy endpoint, the incidence of donor chimerism (> 50% T cell) and the level of chimerism by visit, and change in participant-perceived quality of life. Evaluate outcomes in participants who are only transiently chimeric and evaluate the incidence of acute rejection, death, renal graft loss, and lost to follow-up in participants who did not achieve durable chimerism.

narrativeContent.name: Data Quality Assurance
narrativeContent.description: Sponsor staff and/or its designee review the data entered in the CRFs by investigational site staff for completeness and accuracy and instruct the site personnel to make any required corrections or additions. Site staff are required to respond to any queries received and confirm or correct the data. Concomitant medications will be coded using the World Health Organization Drug Reference List with Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification system. Concomitant procedures, non-drug therapies, and AEs will be coded using MedDRA terminology. Results from laboratory samples tested centrally will be sent electronically to the sponsor.

narrativeContent.name: Protocol Adherence
narrativeContent.description: This protocol defines the study objectives, the study procedures, and the data to be collected on study participants. Additional assessments required to ensure safety of participants should be conducted if considered necessary on a case-by-case basis. Investigators ascertain they will apply due diligence to avoid protocol deviations; all significant deviations will be recorded and reported in the clinical study report. If an investigator believes that a protocol deviation would improve the conduct of the study for safety reasons, this must be considered a protocol amendment.

narrativeContent.name: Protocol Amendments
narrativeContent.description: Any change or addition to the protocol can only be made in a written protocol amendment that must be approved by the sponsor and the IRB prior to implementation. Only amendments that are intended to eliminate an apparent immediate hazard to participants can be implemented immediately, provided health authorities are subsequently notified by protocol amendment and the reviewing IRB is notified. The investigator is expected to take any immediate action required for the safety of any participant in this study, even if the action represents a deviation from the protocol.

narrativeContent.name: Ethics Compliance
narrativeContent.description: This clinical study was designed and will be implemented and reported in accordance with ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki, International Conference on Harmonization GCP, and all applicable regulatory requirements.

narrativeContent.name: Institutional Review Board
narrativeContent.description: Before the study starts, the investigator and institution must obtain IRB approval for the protocol, ICF, recruitment materials and procedures, and any other written information provided to potential participants. Written IRB approval must be submitted to the sponsor prior to enrolling a participant into the study. The Principal Investigator must sign the Investigator's Agreement and is responsible for informing the IRB any amendment to the protocol in accordance with local requirements. The protocol must be re-approved by the IRB upon receipt of amendments and annually, as local regulations require.

narrativeContent.name: Informed Consent
narrativeContent.description: The Principal Investigator will ensure that the patient is given full and adequate oral and written information about the nature, purpose, and possible risks and benefits of the study. Patients must also be notified that they are free to discontinue from the study at any time. Women of childbearing potential should be informed that the study treatment may involve unknown risks to the fetus if pregnancy were to occur during the study and agree to adhere to the contraception requirement. The participant's signed and dated informed consent must be obtained before conducting any study procedures. Donor informed consent will be obtained by the NMDP.

narrativeContent.name: Participant and Data Confidentiality
narrativeContent.description: After the ICF has been signed, each participant will be assigned a unique identifier. To ensure confidentiality of records and personal data of participants, any participant records or datasets transferred to the sponsor will only include the identifier. The names of participants or any information that would make the participant identifiable will not be transferred. The participant must be informed that his/her personal study-related data will be used by the sponsor in accordance with local data protection law and that his/her medical records may be examined by research quality assurance auditors or other authorized personnel appointed by the sponsor, by appropriate IRB members, and by inspectors from regulatory authorities.

narrativeContent.name: Inspection of Records
narrativeContent.description: The sponsor will be allowed to conduct site visits to the investigation facilities for the purpose of monitoring any aspect of the study. The investigator agrees to allow the monitor to inspect the investigational product storage area and accountability records, participant charts, study source documents, and other records relative to study conduct.

narrativeContent.name: Site Monitoring
narrativeContent.description: Before the study starts, at a site initiation visit or at an investigator's meeting, a sponsor representative and/or designee will review the protocol and CRFs with the investigators and their staff. During the study, the sponsor will ensure compliance with the protocol and Good Clinical Practice as well as the quality and integrity of the data at each site. The Clinical Research Associate will visit the site to check the completeness of participant records, the accuracy of entries on the CRFs, the adherence to the protocol, and to GCP, the progress of enrollment, and to ensure that investigational product is being stored, administered, and accounted for according to specifications.

narrativeContent.name: Study Completion and Site Closure
narrativeContent.description: Upon completion of the study, the monitor will conduct the following activities in conjunction with the investigator or study site personnel: return of all study data to the sponsor, data queries, accountability and reconciliation of investigational product, review of study records for completeness, and reconciliation of Investigator Site File and Trial Master File.

narrativeContent.name: Access to Information for Audits and Inspections
narrativeContent.description: Authorized representatives of the sponsor, a regulatory authority, or an IRB may visit the site to perform audits or inspections, including source data verification. The purpose of a sponsor audit or inspection is to systematically and independently examine all study-related activities and documents to determine whether these activities were conducted, and data were recorded, analyzed, and accurately reported according to the protocol, GCP, and any applicable regulatory requirements. The investigator should contact the sponsor immediately if contacted by a regulatory agency about an inspection.
narrativeContent.sectionTitle: Access to Information for Audits and Inspections

narrativeContent.name: Retention of Records
narrativeContent.description: The Principal Investigator must maintain all documentation relating to the study for a period of 2 years after the last marketing application approval, or if not approved, 2 years following the discontinuance of the test article for investigation. If it becomes necessary for the sponsor or a regulatory authority to review any documentation relating to the study, the investigator must permit access to such records.

narrativeContent.name: Publication and Data Sharing Policy
narrativeContent.description: No data collected as part of the study will be utilized in any written work, including publications, without the written consent of the sponsor. The sponsor will post key design elements of this protocol in a publicly accessible database such as clinicaltrials.gov. Upon study completion and finalization of the study report, the results of the trial will be either submitted for publication and/or posted in a publicly accessible database of clinical trial results.

statisticalAnalysis.name: Primary and Secondary Statistical Analysis
statisticalAnalysis.label: Statistical Analysis Plan
statisticalAnalysis.description: Statistical methods were not taken into consideration in determining the sample size. The primary efficacy endpoint will be summarized using a point estimate along with its 95% confidence interval (CI) (exact binomial). Participants who are not free from IS at Month 15 or having BPAR, or graft loss, or death will be considered non-responders. The key secondary efficacy variable is the change in renal function (eGFR by CKD-EPI 2021), from baseline (Day −9, prior to the first dose of transplantation conditioning) to Month 15. Because this is a proof-of-concept study, no hypothesis tests will be conducted on the key secondary efficacy endpoint. Categorical endpoints will be summarized using counts and proportions. Endpoints with continuous variables will be summarized descriptively (non-missing values, means, standard deviations, medians, 25% and 75% quartiles, minimums, and maximums).
statisticalAnalysis.primaryModel: Descriptive statistics with 95% confidence intervals (exact binomial)

concomitantMedications.name: Concomitant Medications
concomitantMedications.label: Study Concomitant Medications
concomitantMedications.description: All medications, procedures, and significant non-drug therapies administered after the participant has signed the study informed consent form will be recorded on the relevant case report form. The investigator should instruct the participant to notify the study site about any new medications, including non-prescription supplements, taken after study enrollment. Concomitant medications entered into the database will be coded using the World Health Organization Drug Reference List, which employs the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification system.

permitted.name: Bacterial Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Bacterial prophylaxis must be provided at least from Day 1 until the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is >500 cells/µL. Specific antibacterials may be given according to center practice. An example is moxifloxacin 400 mg per day.

permitted.name: Fungal Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Fungal prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until the ANC is >500 cells/µL. Specific antifungals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement but must include coverage of molds such as Aspergillus. An example is posaconazole 300 mg daily.

permitted.name: Viral Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until Day 183 and is recommended until Month 12. Specific antivirals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement. An example is valacyclovir 500 mg twice a day. For participants who are immunoglobulin G (IgG) (+) for CMV and participants who are IgG (−) for CMV but who received a kidney from a donor who is IgG (+), it is recommended that CMV prophylaxis be provided from Day 1 until Day 92. An example is letermovir 480 mg once daily.
permitted.condition: From Day 1 until Day 183 (recommended until Month 12)

permitted.name: Pneumocystis Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Pneumocystis prophylaxis (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia/pneumocystis carinii pneumonia) must be provided starting on Day 22 or after the ANC is >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later. If the CD4 count at the Day 183 visit is >200 cells/µL, the pneumocystis prophylaxis may be discontinued. If the CD4 count is ≤ 200 cells/µL, the agent should be continued until the CD4 count check at Month 12. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 single strength tablet daily is the preferred example, with atovaquone 1500 mg once daily or dapsone 100 mg once daily as alternatives.
permitted.condition: Starting Day 22 or after ANC >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later

permitted.name: Premedication for IF001 Infusion
permitted.description: Premedication with corticosteroids (100 mg hydrocortisone), diphenhydramine, and acetaminophen should be performed as prophylaxis against adverse infusion-related side effects per institutional guidelines.

permitted.name: Infusion Reaction Management
permitted.description: If nausea and/or headache is reported by the recipient due to DMSO, reduce the rate of infusion and administer ondansetron and/or diphenhydramine (if indicated). Wait 10-15 minutes before thawing and infusing subsequent bags of donor cells.
permitted.condition: During IF001 infusion if reactions occur

permitted.name: Brief Systemic Corticosteroids
permitted.description: Brief use of systemic corticosteroids for no more than 8 weeks (total duration) if administered for an indication other than rejection prophylaxis or treatment (such as newly developed or recurrent autoimmune diseases, asthma, hypersensitivity reactions).
permitted.condition: For indications other than rejection prophylaxis or treatment, maximum 8 weeks total duration

prohibited.name: Non-Thymoglobulin ATG Preparations
prohibited.description: Preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) other than Thymoglobulin are excluded from the conditioning regimen and are not permitted during the study.

prohibited.name: Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta)
prohibited.description: Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta®) is not permitted during the study. Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar should be used instead for granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support.

prohibited.name: Granulocyte-macrophage-CSF
prohibited.description: Granulocyte-macrophage-CSF is not permitted during the study. Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar should be used instead for granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support.

dataMonitoringCommittee.name: Data Safety Monitoring Board
dataMonitoringCommittee.label: DSMB
dataMonitoringCommittee.description: An independent data safety monitoring board (DSMB) will be instituted at study initiation to advise the sponsor and investigators on matters relating to the safety and conduct of the study. The DSMB will be governed by a charter that includes meeting frequency, stopping rules, and event triggers necessitating unscheduled reviews. The DSMB will oversee the safety and risk/benefit of the study and follow stopping rules as defined in the DSMB Charter. Further enrollment will be temporarily halted for full DSMB safety assessment if specific safety thresholds are met, including severe acute GVHD in participants, BPAR events, Grade 3-4 infusion reactions, prolonged neutropenia, organ toxicity, or any death or graft loss. The DSMB will critically assess the background and clinical course of events leading to study temporary halt as soon as possible.
dataMonitoringCommittee.mandate: Advise the sponsor and investigators on matters relating to the safety and conduct of the study
dataMonitoringCommittee.charter: A charter that will include meeting frequency, stopping rules, and event triggers necessitating an unscheduled review

labValueThresholds.label: ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days

cellTherapyManufacturing.name: IF001 Cell Therapy Manufacturing
cellTherapyManufacturing.label: IF001 Manufacturing Process
cellTherapyManufacturing.description: IF001 is an investigational cell therapy product containing defined doses of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and alpha/beta positive T-cell receptor (αβ TCR) cells for induction of transplantation tolerance in recipients of kidney transplants from the same donor. The cryopreserved product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW (no maximum) and a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). Freshly harvested donor stem cells are immediately transported to the manufacturing center where the IF001 product is manufactured, cryopreserved, and stored prior to shipping to the study center for thawing and infusion into the participant. The IF001 product must pass applicable release criteria and is shipped frozen to the treating center prior to Day −9.
cellTherapyManufacturing.collectionProcedure: granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilization and apheresis
cellTherapyManufacturing.collectionTiming: The same living kidney donor will undergo G-CSF mobilization and apheresis to generate the IF001 product
cellTherapyManufacturing.minimumStemCellYield: minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW
cellTherapyManufacturing.manufacturingNotes: Donors will undergo stem cell mobilization, stem cell collection, and follow-up according to NMDP standard procedures. The sponsor has contracted with the National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) to manage the donation process and donor follow-up.

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Thymoglobulin
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Anti-thymocyte globulin
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Thymoglobulin (anti-thymocyte globulin) is administered as part of the reduced intensity conditioning regimen. Given on Days -9 (0.5 mg/kg intravenously over 6 hours), -8 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours), and -7 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours). Preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin other than Thymoglobulin are excluded from the study protocol.

agents.name: Thymoglobulin
agents.dose: 0.5 mg/kg on Day -9, 2 mg/kg on Days -8 and -7

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Fludarabine
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Fludarabine conditioning
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Fludarabine is administered on Days -6, -5, -4, -3 and -2 at 30 mg/m2 IV daily, with dose adjusted for kidney function. Dosed on body surface area based upon recipient's actual body weight if <125% of IBW. For participants >125% of IBW, dosed on adjusted IBW. For participants with estimated or measured creatinine clearance <70 mL/min/1.73 m2, prior brain radiation, or prior intrathecal chemotherapy, the dose should be reduced by 20%.

agents.name: Fludarabine
agents.dose: 30 mg/m2 IV daily (dose adjusted for kidney function)

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Pre-transplantation Cyclophosphamide
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Pre-transplant cyclophosphamide
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Pre-transplantation cyclophosphamide is administered on Day -6 and Day -5 at 14.5 mg/kg IV daily as a 1- to 2-hour infusion. The total dose received is 29 mg/kg over the two days. This is part of the reduced intensity conditioning regimen administered prior to IF001 infusion.

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Total Body Irradiation
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: TBI conditioning
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: A single fraction of total body irradiation (TBI) treatment is administered on Day -1. The dose is 200 cGy for the HLA-matched cohort and 400 cGy for the partially HLA-matched cohort. This is the final component of the reduced intensity conditioning regimen before IF001 infusion on Day 1.

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Acute GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.label: Acute GVHD Assessment
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Monitoring for acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) with characterization of incidence and grade by Day 120 post-IF001 infusion. All Grade >2 acute GVHD will be reported within 24 hours of site awareness as an adverse event of special interest (AESI). Evaluation includes assessment at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15 for incidence and grade of acute GVHD.
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.notes: Grade >2 acute GVHD reported as AESI within 24 hours

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Chronic GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.label: Chronic GVHD Assessment
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Monitoring for chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) with characterization of incidence and severity by one-year post-IF001 infusion. Any chronic GVHD will be reported within 24 hours of site awareness as an adverse event of special interest (AESI). Evaluation includes assessment at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15 for incidence and severity of chronic GVHD. Extended evaluation continues at Months 18 and 24.
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.notes: Any chronic GVHD reported as AESI within 24 hours

priorTherapyRequirements.name: No extensive prior T cell-depleting therapy
priorTherapyRequirements.label: Limited T cell depletion
priorTherapyRequirements.description: Participants enrolled in the RELIEF trial will be similar to those treated by DeZern et al. in that they will not have received extensive prior therapy with T cell-depleting agents or received multiple rounds of IS chemotherapies. This requirement ensures that participants have not been heavily pretreated with immunosuppressive agents that could interfere with the tolerance induction protocol.
priorTherapyRequirements.prohibitedPriorEvents: extensive prior therapy with T cell-depleting agents or received multiple rounds of IS chemotherapies

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: CD34+ Cell Dose Requirement
stemCellCollectionRequirements.label: Minimum CD34+ cells
stemCellCollectionRequirements.description: The cryopreserved IF001 product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient ideal body weight (IBW) with no maximum limit. This minimum dose is set above the lowest dose given in the DeZern et al. (2023) trial, where all 20 patients conditioned with 400 cGy TBI achieved engraftment and stable long-term donor chimerism. Higher CD34+ cell doses are associated with faster neutrophil and platelet recovery and lower risk of graft failure, with doses greater than 3.2 million/kg showing significantly lower graft failure rates (11% versus 31%) in aplastic anemia patients receiving HLA-haploidentical grafts.
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 3 million CD34+ cells per kg recipient IBW
stemCellCollectionRequirements.rationaleForMinimum: Set above lowest dose in DeZern 2023 trial where all patients achieved engraftment; higher doses associated with faster recovery and lower graft failure rates
stemCellCollectionRequirements.timing: Collection occurs after G-CSF mobilization of living kidney donor

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: αβ TCR Cell Dose Requirement
stemCellCollectionRequirements.label: Target αβ TCR cells
stemCellCollectionRequirements.description: The IF001 product contains a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). This dose was chosen to minimize the incidence of severe acute or chronic GVHD while simultaneously reducing the incidence of graft failure and opportunistic infection. The dosing considers risks of acute and chronic GVHD with high αβ TCR cell doses versus risks of non-engraftment and infection with low αβ TCR cell doses. In the DeZern 2023 study, patients received a median of 5.1 x 10^7 CD3+ cells/kg with low GVHD rates (7% acute Grade 2, 4% chronic).
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 8-12 million αβ TCR cells per kg recipient IBW
stemCellCollectionRequirements.rationaleForMinimum: Balance between minimizing GVHD risk and preventing graft failure and opportunistic infections
stemCellCollectionRequirements.timing: Collection occurs after G-CSF mobilization of living kidney donor

siteManagement.name: Multicenter Study Site Management
siteManagement.label: Multicenter US Sites
siteManagement.siteType: Multiple centers in the United States
siteManagement.description: Study IF001-CL201 is a Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study conducted at multiple centers in the United States. The Principal Investigator and at least 2 staff from each site will need to complete training requirements and obtain access to the electronic data capture system (Advantage eClinical managed by Emmes). Site monitoring includes pre-study site initiation visits, ongoing monitoring visits by Clinical Research Associates to check completeness of participant records, accuracy of CRF entries, adherence to protocol and Good Clinical Practice, progress of enrollment, and proper investigational product storage and administration. Centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes to the CIBMTR using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database.

longTermFollowUp.name: Long-term Follow-up
longTermFollowUp.label: Long-term Follow-up
longTermFollowUp.description: Study completion is defined as the point at which all ongoing IF001 recipients have completed the Month 15 visit. The investigator must provide follow-up medical care for all participants who are prematurely withdrawn from the study or must refer them for appropriate ongoing care according to local practice. This includes reporting to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) and follow-up in appropriate national registries (eg, United Network for Organ Sharing, etc.). Centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes to the CIBMTR. Registration is done using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database. Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients. The CIBMTR forms will be submitted directly to the CIBMTR through routine CIBMTR mechanisms.
longTermFollowUp.regulatoryBasis: Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients
longTermFollowUp.infrastructure: Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) and appropriate national registries (eg, United Network for Organ Sharing, etc.)
longTermFollowUp.protocol: Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database procedures and forms
longTermFollowUp.notes: CIBMTR forms will be submitted directly to the CIBMTR through routine CIBMTR mechanisms
